title: Evaluate our food design
outcome: FOODWISE: evaluate taste, cost and nutrition.
goal: I can use real evidence to review my dish, check its cost and choose one improvement.
success: I can separate a taste note from an appearance note.
I can check cost per portion and describe the food groups.
I can give one improvement with a reason linked to my evidence.
safety_boundary: No food is needed today. Do not bring or taste the Week 2 food a week later. Use the actual Week 2 notes or a checked food-only photo. If taste was not tried and recorded, write taste not assessed. A photo cannot prove taste. Any fresh tasting would be a separate, newly cleared food activity and is not required here.
cost_basis: Week 1 model prices are invented for the stated amounts used by one person. They are not whole-pack shopping prices. The 60 g yoghurt is counted once, split as about 20 g in the filling and 40 g alongside. Use the pupil’s actual approved ingredient amounts and substitutions. Unknown costs stay unknown.
cost_examples: 280p batch cost divided by 2 actual portions
nutrition: Variety contributes to a balanced eating pattern.
Dairy provides calcium; a suitable alternative needs label and dietary checks.
Small amounts of oils and spreads
No added oil in this cold model
Do not add oil just to fill a box.
nutrition_note: Balance is built across the day or week. Each meal does not need exact plate sections. Use the actual dish and amounts in your review. These example portions do not meet every person’s needs. Choose water as a drink. No calorie counting, body or weight discussion is needed.
review_steps: Find the actual plan, cost record, safe-working notes and any checked food-only photo. Name what is present and what is missing.
Use a recorded taste note only for taste. Use a photo or actual plate record for appearance. Recheck the portion cost and food groups.
Name a real strength or limit, then one useful change and why. Say how you would check whether the change helped.
fallback: With no prior food record, make an honest gap record. Review the clearly labelled adult cost model for practice and keep the pupil’s actual dish evaluation pending. With no paper or device, give an oral or signed review and have an adult record exact confirmed words when possible. Mark transcription pending until it exists. No kitchen, food or tasting is needed.
evidence: The pupil’s own review states the dish and actual source, taste assessed from the recorded Week 2 note or taste not assessed, appearance if evidenced, checked cost per portion, food-group comment and one improvement with a reason. Keep the date, evidence location and actual support. Missing evidence and simulation remain clearly marked.

Supported: Read or hear your actual record with an adult. Mark any gap.
Choose taste note, appearance note or not assessed for each claim.
Use pence to check one portion with a calculator or adult.
Say one food-group comment and one improvement with a reason.
Standard: Use your actual plan and Week 2 record or photo.
Check taste status and appearance separately.
Recalculate ingredient-use cost per portion and review the food groups.
Give one improvement, a reason and a way to check it next time.
Stretch: Complete the core honest review first.
Compare the actual dish with the Week 1 design and explain a real change.
Cost a second version or show the effect of portion number on a batch cost.
Weigh cost, likely practical demands and food-group balance. Keep predictions separate from findings.

vocabulary: How food helps meet our needs.
A change intended to make the next version work better.

adaptations.Cognition and Learning: Show one review heading at a time. Read the actual record aloud. Model the first cost addition, then fade. Keep all amounts in pence before converting to pounds. Use a calculator and a food-group list.
adaptations.Communication and Interaction: Accept pointing, speech, signing, drawing or pupil-directed scribing. Ask one short question and allow thinking time. Read the review back so the pupil can confirm or correct it.
adaptations.SEMH: Keep food preferences and evidence private. No compulsory tasting, body or weight talk, home-finance questions or public rankings. Offer a calm pause and an agreed return cue. Keep feedback about the design.
adaptations.Sensory and Physical: No food contact or tasting is required. Offer a large-print view and verbal description of any actual photo. A pupil who did not taste records taste not assessed and can still review cost, appearance and food groups.
adaptations.EAL: Plan and explain in any language. Pair each review word with a short example. Read money and quantities aloud. Confirm the meaning of the pupil’s own words before scribing or translation.

careers: Food designers and catering teams compare evidence, cost and nutrition before changing a recipe. An honest review helps the next person make a better version.

stages.name: Arrival
stages.title: Our actual records
pupil: Find your Week 1 plan and Week 2 evidence.
Use notes or a checked food-only photo.
No food or tasting is needed today.
stages.teacher: State the no-old-food rule before opening records. Check what actually exists: plan, ingredient-use prices, preparation note and optional food-only photo. Keep identifying images private and do not project them. Missing items stay missing. Use a quiet settling minute inside this stage.
stages.check: Ask: Do we need last week’s food? No. We use records. If an item is absent, note the gap rather than replacing it with a generated model.

stages.name: Starter
stages.title: Taste or appearance
pupil: Sort a taste note from an appearance note.
A photo can show appearance.
Taste not tried and recorded means taste not assessed.
stages.teacher: Use adult examples only: a recorded note says mild flavour; a photo shows a folded wrap; no taste note means taste not assessed. Let pupils point, speak or sign the category. Do not invite guesses about taste from a picture.
stages.check: A visible folded edge is appearance. A recorded flavour is taste. A photo alone cannot prove flavour.

stages.name: I do
stages.title: An honest adult review
pupil: Watch the review claim being matched to its source.
See the one-portion costs checked once.
Hear a change explained as a prediction.
stages.teacher: Model with an adult example: I have only the model cost card, so I cannot claim a pupil’s taste. Add 35+30+15+10+20+30=140p. Say £1.40 is already per portion. Do not divide it again. Show the two-portion batch example separately. Fade by leaving the last addition for pupils.
stages.check: Ask: Is 140p already one portion or a whole batch of unknown size? It is the one-portion model. A model review never replaces the pupil’s actual evidence.

stages.name: We do
stages.title: Cost and food groups
pupil: Check the model total and money left.
Match the ingredients to food groups.
Use your own actual changes when you review.
stages.teacher: Work through the food-group table and explain balance across a day or week. Check the apple-to-pear example: 140 minus 30 plus 35 is 145p. Distinguish ingredient-use prices from whole packs. Explain 280p divided by two actual portions gives 140p each. Use an actual approved substitution only if its amount and price are known.
stages.check: Model total £1.40, budget left 60p. Pear version £1.45, 55p left. A two-portion £2.80 batch is £1.40 per portion. No invented amount is added to a pupil’s record.

stages.name: We do 2
stages.title: A claim we can support
pupil: There is a photo but no recorded taste note.
Choose: taste proved, taste not assessed, or taste copied from a friend.
Use the evidence before making a claim.
stages.teacher: Correct hinge answer is taste not assessed. If any pupil chooses another answer, stop the claim, separate the evidence types and reteach. Parallel check: a £2.80 batch made two portions. Cost per portion is £1.40, not £2.80 or 70p. A quiz answer does not supply missing evidence.
stages.check: Move to the pupil review after they can keep a photo claim separate from a taste claim. Use the Supported route and calculator for an uncertain cost check.

stages.name: Independent
stages.title: My evaluation
pupil: In your book, name your dish and the evidence you used.
Review taste status, appearance, cost and food groups.
Choose one improvement and give a reason.
stages.teacher: Use one route and the evaluation prompts. The pupil’s own review should point to the actual record. If taste is unassessed, write that and continue with other headings. Ask what one real feature or constraint suggests a change. Predictions about the next version are labelled predictions. Scribe exact pupil words and read them back. Use a quiet organisation minute inside this stage.
stages.check: Look for a checked cost per portion, one food-group comment, honest taste status and one improvement linked to a reason. Record actual support and any evidence still pending.

stages.name: Review
stages.title: Check the reason
pupil: Check every claim against its source.
Read or hear your own improvement reason.
Correct one part if needed.
stages.teacher: Offer an opt-in partner check or a private adult review. A useful comment asks which evidence supports a claim and how the change might help. The pupil decides and records a correction. Keep sensory judgements neutral and personal. Tidy and store actual records in the final minute.
stages.check: Accept a truthful limited review. Do not change taste not assessed into a score or invent a successful dish.

stages.name: Exit
stages.title: My next version
pupil: My cost per portion was ___ or is still unknown.
One thing my evidence shows is ___.
I would change ___ because ___.
stages.teacher: Keep the completed review with the plan and actual making evidence. Record one next step and any gap. The next strand uses textiles. Do not claim that a proposed food change has already been made or tasted.
stages.check: Retain the pupil’s own reason, date, evidence location and support. A spoken or signed review can be confirmed to a scribe.

misconceptions: It shows appearance. Use a recorded taste note or mark taste not assessed.
Divide £1.40 by two because two pupils are present.
£1.40 is already the model cost for one portion. Divide only a whole batch cost by its actual portion count.
A balanced review must say the dish was perfect.
It can name a useful strength, a limit and one improvement. Balance builds across the day or week.
An adult model can fill a missing pupil record.
Label the model as practice and keep the pupil’s actual evaluation pending.
